In less than 30 months, Los Angeles went from a roster packed with familiar faces to a total franchise reset.

The biggest shift is the end of the LeBron James and Anthony Davis era. 

For years, everything in L.A. revolved around LeBron and AD. Moving on from both megastars officially closes the book on the chapter that brought the 2020 championship to the Staples Center. 

Along with them, the entire supporting cast has moved on.

In their place, the Lakers ushered in a brand-new timeline. 

Acquiring Luka Dončić completely reshaped the organization's identity, giving them a generational primary playmaker to run the offense. They now also brought in 7-foot-2 big man Walker Kessler, locking down the paint and giving Luka an elite rim-protecting lob threat.
